statement.excerpt: It intends to spend $50 billion or more on compute this year, which I estimate is more than 50% of all global AI compute spend (with OpenAI taking up 50%+ of all AI compute infrastructure).

from_speaker: intends to spend $50 billion or more on compute
more than 50% of all global AI compute spend
our_interpretation: Assess the estimate of calendar-year 2026 spending plans asserted at publication, rather than a forecast of completed year-end spending.
The central proposition is OpenAI's share of global spending. Verifying its own budget alone does not verify that share.
A comparable denominator must avoid counting both cloud customers' payments and the providers' underlying capital purchases as separate final expenditure.
The infrastructure parenthesis describes physical capacity and requires a separate measure; spending share cannot establish it.
The spending classification denotes a full-year budget rather than an annualized revenue or expenditure run rate.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable contemporaneous estimates establish an OpenAI 2026 compute budget of at least USD 50 billion and a share strictly above 50% of worldwide AI compute spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence establishes a budget below USD 50 billion or a spending share of 50% or less.
